label: Amphibian / Frog (order Anura), representative: American bullfrog

image.species_shown: Lithobates catesbeianus, adult male, Plaisance National Park, Quebec (June 2012), per Commons ImageDescription
image.view: not visually confirmed; Commons categories list 'Amphibians facing left' and water reflections. Image download was refused with HTTP 429 on upload.wikimedia.org, and thumb.wikimedia.org is blocked by the egress proxy.

physical_parsing.volume_method: Ellipsoid for the trunk and head (semi-axes 0.045 x 0.025 x 0.065 m, about 0.0003 m3, roughly 0.3 kg at density ~1). Limbs are excluded as they are thin and add little volume. Bounding box assumes a resting, crouched posture with legs folded, giving about 0.12 m across the spread hind knees, 0.07 m high and 0.20 m snout-to-toe.
physical_parsing.shape_class: squat ovoid body (dorsoventrally flattened, wider than tall) with a broad head fused to the trunk and splayed, folded hind limbs

core.description: Single fused head-trunk ellipsoid. Pectoral girdle and pelvis sit inside the trunk at the forelimb and hind-limb roots. Head is continuous with the trunk, with no neck. Rear of the trunk is the urostyle/pelvic region.
core.cross_section: ellipse, roughly 0.09 m wide by 0.05 m high at mid-trunk

physical_parsing.size_source: Typical adult: SVL 0.09-0.15 m (up to about 0.20 m in records). Mean SVL 0.152 m for males and 0.162 m for females (AmphibiaWeb, species 4999, via search results). Wikipedia gives 9-15 cm SVL. Hind-limb reach estimated at about 0.17 m extended, ~0.09 m folded, from typical Rana/Lithobates limb proportions. Limb and eye sizes are approximate and not taken from a source.

parts.name: Hind leg (femur, tibia-fibula, tarsus), left

penetration.overlap_region: Pelvic/ilium girdle at the posterior-lateral trunk, around the hip socket. Deep enough to seat the femoral head inside the core.

parts.notes: The key jumping structure. Hind legs are long: about 1.5-2x body length extended and folded to the trunk at rest. Femur, tibiofibula and tarsus are the main segments, with the knee flexing about 90-120 degrees for jumping. Joint pivots and ranges are estimates from general frog hind-limb kinematics, not measurements. Sources: general anuran morphology references; no specific source was retrieved for joint ranges.

parts.name: Hind foot, webbed (5 toes with interdigital web), left

penetration.overlap_region: Distal end of the tarsal segment of hind_leg_L. The foot is a terminal extension, so it only needs to seat into the tarsus.

parts.notes: Long, broad, five-toed foot with interdigital webbing used for push-off and swimming. Terminal part of the hind-limb chain.

parts.name: Fore leg with four free digits, left

penetration.overlap_region: Pectoral girdle (scapulocoracoid) at the anterior-lateral trunk, under the shoulder skin.

parts.notes: Short, slender forelimbs with four unwebbed digits. Used to prop up the body, absorb landing shock and, in males, for amplexus (clasping the female, with nuptial pads on the first digit). Classed as manipulation because the main function is grasping. Lengths and joint ranges are approximate.

parts.name: Protruding eye (dorsal, bulging), left

penetration.overlap_region: Dorsal cranium around the orbit. The eye is seated into the skull so it does not float.

parts.notes: Dorsally placed, bulging eyes give near-360 degree vision above the water surface while the body is submerged. Eye size is approximate.

parts.name: Tympanum (external eardrum disc), left

penetration.overlap_region: Lateral head surface directly behind the eye, over the otic capsule.

parts.notes: Flat, round membrane behind each eye, used for airborne sound reception. Large in male bullfrogs, which are also larger than females. Size is approximate.

parts.name: Wide mouth (gape with lip margin)

penetration.overlap_region: Anterior face of the skull. Nearly flush, so the mouth is a surface opening and not a protruding part.

parts.notes: Very wide, almost circular gape that reaches the eye line. Gape is about 1/3 of the head width. Part is a surface feature with a small geometric footprint.

parts.name: Projectile tongue (hyoid-attached)

penetration.overlap_region: Floor of the mouth at the anterior hyoid, inside the head core. Attached at the front, not the tip, so it flips out ballistically.

parts.notes: Long, sticky tongue attached to the front of the lower jaw and flipped forward to catch prey. Extension is hydrostatic/ballistic and fast. Not covered by the library.

parts.name: Vocal sac (throat resonator)

penetration.overlap_region: Ventral throat wall of the head-trunk core.

parts.notes: Male bullfrog throat sac, which inflates to amplify the call. It is communicative, so the category is debatable. It is placed under sensory as an acoustic interface, but it could equally be aesthetics (display). Size is approximate.

constraints.symmetry: bilateral about the sagittal (X=0) plane; midline parts (mouth, tongue, vocal sac) are centre
constraints.gait: saltatory jump: simultaneous extension of both hind limbs for launch, forelimbs for landing absorption. Swimming uses synchronized hind-leg kicks with the webbed feet.
other: Forelimbs are short and cannot contribute to jumping thrust; do not model them as the primary locomotor.
Eyes are seated dorsally, so the eye part must sit on the top of the head (higher y), not the front.
Mouth is a near-surface feature: it is not a deep penetration, but the jaw hinge pivot is used for gape animation.
Tympanum and vocal sac are sound-related and should be handled together if the model includes voice.

library_gaps.why: No library part models a long segmented jumping leg. foot_webbed covers only the terminal foot, so the leg chain is a gap.
No library part for a flat, circular membrane set behind the eye. ear_leaf is a flap and does not fit.
No library part for a long, sticky, ballistically extended tongue attached at the hyoid.
No library part for an inflatable throat membrane. The closest is bulge, which is cosmetic and does not match the functional role.
